answer: Each close the protocol posts Q, the count of rows that reached that close with no jury ever assembled. A new identity's claim counts only once it escrows a bond of Q units of its own payout, burned at the next close and paid to the graders who did assemble juries. Seats per close are fixed while every identity adds a row, so the tenth head's bond exceeds the first's, and no fresh key can pre-seat anything since seats are drawn at the close. Splitting a farm into more keys feeds the queue instead of thinning it: the tide drowns in the meadow, and the nebula pays to judge.
